dod_intent_evidence: AFWERX STRATFI $30M+$30M match award (2024), SBIR Phase II ~$12M for ATARS Integration on AFSOC MC-130J (2025, sbir.gov), and a direct U.S. Air Force contract via Air Combat Command to integrate ATARS into the F-16 (Aug 2025 press release) — deep, repeated DoD motion in the company's own press.
score_evidence: 'We are warfighters, engineers and technologists... driven by the personal passion of our founder and CEO to solve a national security problem that is threatening the readiness of our warfighters' → operator_absence low, operators central to identity

Open roles include 'Trade Compliance/Export Controls Manager' and 'Configuration Management (CM) Manager' → hiring_profile_skew low, they are hiring deployment/compliance roles not just lab researchers
Site copy is entirely mission/vision language ('A revolutionary approach to military flight training is urgently needed') with zero accuracy%/fps/TRL bragging → lab_language_intensity low

blind_spots.blind_spot: ATARS is pitched as an 'AI-enabled 3D synthetic training world' that lets 'humans and machines train together...at scale in realistic threat environments' with no mention anywhere on-site of how the system performs when comms are degraded at a remote or forward training range.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A live-rendered AR overlay in a cockpit depends on continuous low-latency data; if the training range's network drops or degrades, the pilot loses the synthetic threat picture mid-sortie — the same DDIL failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case, just airborne.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company narrative is built around the AR/training-realism vision and the founder's fighter-pilot story, not network architecture, so DDIL resilience isn't part of the public pitch even if solved internally.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'a fully immersive, data-driven, AI-enabled 3D synthetic training world that allows humans and machines to train together safely, frequently, and at scale'

blind_spots.blind_spot: No public discussion of SWaP-C for the AR hardware actually worn/mounted in an F-16 or MC-130J cockpit, despite now having live integration contracts on both airframes.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Cockpit space, power budget, and weight margins on legacy fighter/transport platforms are notoriously tight; an AR headset or HUD-injection system that isn't co-designed against those constraints from day one risks integration rework late in the contract.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Public materials are aimed at recruiting and press, not engineering disclosure, so SWaP-C tradeoffs on specific airframes stay internal.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Red 6 Secures U.S. Air Force Contract to Revolutionize F-16 Pilot Training with World-First Augmented Reality Training System'

blind_spots.blind_spot: Company-level CMMC/NIST 800-171 posture is never mentioned on-site, despite handling ITAR-controlled flight-training and avionics-integration data across multiple USAF programs.
blind_spots.operator_reality: One Air Force contracting officer's CMMC audit finding can freeze a payment milestone regardless of how well the product itself performs — the compliance posture, not the tech, becomes the valley-of-death risk at this stage.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The hiring of a Trade Compliance/Export Controls Manager shows they're aware of the ITAR side, but CMMC/NIST 800-171 readiness isn't surfaced publicly the way it is for pure-software vendors.

opener_hook: Red 6 just added an F-16 integration contract via Air Combat Command to its MC-130J STRATFI award — two different airframe integrations running in parallel is exactly where deployment architecture debt compounds fastest.
what_they_do: Augmented-reality synthetic flight training system (ATARS) that overlays live threat simulations into a pilot's real cockpit view, now being integrated into F-16 and AFSOC MC-130J programs.
